title: ABCE1 facilitates tumour progression via aerobic glycolysis and inhibits cell death in human colorectal cancer cells through the p53 signalling pathway.
authors: Natarajan, Sathan Raj; Krishnamoorthy, Rajapandiyan; Alshuniaber, Mohammad A; Alsulami, Tawfiq S; Gatasheh, Mansour K; Rajagopal, Ponnulakshmi; Palanisamy, Chella Perumal; Govindan, Ramajayam; Veeraraghavan, Vishnu Priya; Jayaraman, Selvaraj
one_liner_zh: 该文研究ABCE1在结直肠癌中通过p53信号通路促进肿瘤进展和有氧糖酵解，仅含分子对接分析，核心是癌症生物学而非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) poses a formidable challenge to global health, necessitating the quest for novel biomarkers to improve therapeutic strategies. This study explores ABCE1 (ATP-binding cassette subfamily E member 1) as a potential biomarker for CRC and delves into its intricate molecular mechanisms. Through integrated bioinformatic analyses, this study underscores the significant oncogenic role of ABCE1 in CRC, opening new avenues for promising therapeutic interventions. Deletion of ABCE1 reduced cell growth, abrogated aerobic glycolysis, and promoted apoptosis in HT-29 and HCT-116 cells. Further validation through experimentation with irinotecan revealed compelling outcomes, including diminished cell growth, induces G1 phase cell cycle arrest, and promotes apoptosis in HCT-116 and HT-29 colorectal cancer cells. ABCE1 KO with irinotecan combined treatment significantly increased the inhibition of cell proliferation and aerobic glycolysis in CRC cells, accentuating the multifaceted role of ABCE1 in CRC progression. Moreover, this work also demonstrated the complex relationship between ABCE1 and the p53 signalling pathway, which was confirmed in experimental assays. These assays also revealed that deletion of ABCE1 with irinotecan might regulate G1 phase cell cycle arrest, inhibit metabolic regulation, and activate the p53 pathway to induce apoptosis in HCT-116 cells. Molecular docking analyses further supported these findings, revealing the strong binding affinity of irinotecan for targets of the p53 signalling cascade. Collectively, these comprehensive insights support the potential therapeutic efficacy of targeting ABCE1 in CRC treatment strategies. Overall, the findings from this study underscore the importance of ABCE1 as a potential biomarker in CRC and illuminate its complex molecular mechanisms. The demonstrated effectiveness of ABCE1 inhibition, particularly through irinotecan, coupled with its interplay with crucial signalling pathways such as p53, highlights its potential as a promising therapeutic option for colorectal cancer treatment.
abstract_zh: 结直肠癌（CRC）对全球健康构成严峻挑战，亟需寻找新型生物标志物以改善治疗策略。本研究探讨ABCE1（ATP结合盒E亚家族成员1）作为CRC潜在生物标志物的可能性，并深入解析其复杂的分子机制。通过整合生物信息学分析，本研究强调了ABCE1在CRC中的显著致癌作用，为有前景的治疗干预开辟了新途径。删除ABCE1可减少HT-29和HCT-116细胞的生长、抑制有氧糖酵解并促进细胞凋亡。通过伊立替康实验进一步验证显示，令人信服的结果包括在HCT-116和HT-29结直肠癌细胞中减少细胞生长、诱导G1期细胞周期阻滞并促进凋亡。ABCE1敲除（KO）联合伊立替康治疗显著增强了CRC细胞中细胞增殖和有氧糖酵解的抑制，凸显了ABCE1在CRC进展中的多方面作用。此外，本研究还展示了ABCE1与p53信号通路之间的复杂关系，并在实验测定中得到证实。这些测定还揭示，ABCE1缺失联合伊立替康可能通过调节G1期细胞周期阻滞、抑制代谢调控并激活p53通路来诱导HCT-116细胞凋亡。分子对接分析进一步支持这些发现，揭示了伊立替康对p53信号级联靶点的强结合亲和力。总体而言，这些全面见解支持靶向ABCE1在CRC治疗策略中的潜在疗效。总之，本研究结果强调了ABCE1作为CRC潜在生物标志物的重要性，并阐明了其复杂的分子机制。ABCE1抑制（尤其是通过伊立替康）所展示的有效性，加上其与p53等关键信号通路的相互作用，凸显了其作为结直肠癌治疗有前景选项的潜力。
